limitations: Image model resynthesis is not a pixel-exact additive composite.
Typography, colors, glyphs, dimensions and component detail are provisional.
Brightest-locale readability remains to be verified with unchanged captures in the HTML rebuild.
Illustrative countdown and ammo values are sample states, not measurements of the captured moment.

concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished whole-screen combat HUD concept over the provided real game screenshot. Preserve the screenshot exactly: same ships, background, camera, brightness, and colors, no repainting or invented world objects. The HUD is projected light seen on invisible canopy glass, never physical cockpit hardware. It only ADDS LIGHT. No dark pixels, dark outlines, shadows, panels, backings, glass edge, reflections, dust, vignette, scene blur or dimming. Keep the scene dominant and empty top-left. Use clean precise warm off-white hairlines, crisp but gently phosphorescent, minimal luminous weight, no busy sci-fi decoration. UI information layout: top center a large countdown "0:19" with three short phase segments under it, no other run stats. Top right a round minimap scope with a thin rim, a few meaningful tiny grey asteroid dots, one teal player chevron and two small coral threat dots, no sweep, no decorative grid or fake readouts. Bottom center one open capabilities cluster: a bold solid geometric keystone symbol inside a circular recovery ring, two weapon arcs flanking it with simple bold filled weapon identity glyphs and small numeric ammo "18" and "6"; two short straight quantity tracks for cyan shield and green hull immediately below this cluster. Tiny quiet bars over the two distant enemy ships. A small thin crosshair near the center. A single bold lavender objective direction glyph near the right screen edge, without a distance readout. Identity glyphs retain bold fill in all variants, interfaces remain hairline. Only 40-degree diagonals for identity glyphs. No words other than "0:19", "18", "6". No headers, option labels, logo or watermark. Keep all text crisp, no text glow. The design is a serene, sleek futuristic projector with 1980s vector-electronics character. Very faint refraction on the outermost scope edge only; never distortion of digits. Full bleed landscape image.
STRATEGY A: VECTOR PHOSPHOR. All instrument tracks and quantities are drawn as luminous thin lines and individual bright tick strokes, with empty scene showing between them. No translucent areas and no area fills except the mandatory bold identity glyphs. The stroke is the material: a precise warm-white hot core with one very narrow faint halo and sparse nearly invisible beam irregularity. This should feel like an elegant original Asteroids vector monitor projected onto a canopy, utterly open and minimal.

NO enclosing rectangular panel, NO dark fill, NO scene blur. Subtle color splitting only on outer arc edges. Preserve exact element positions and sizes of the second reference image, which is only the layout guide; background comes from the first image. The filled keystone identity remains bold.
concepts.correction: Edit only the HUD of this concept. Remove the dark backing behind both bottom capacity bars. Their gaps and empty portions must show the original nebula, with only cyan and green light added by the quantity marks. Keep the faint luminous circular fields behind the three separate bottom instruments and within the map scope. These fields must brighten the scene, never darken it. Preserve all ships, background composition, UI positions and all other design choices. No hardware, shadow or dark fill anywhere on the HUD.
